meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: Level energies are NIST ASD values. 19F: I = 1/2, so only magnetic-dipole constants A exist (no B). The 3d-level A values (Huo et al. 2018) are second-hand from the theory paper arXiv:2108.01116 and carry about 5 % uncertainty. Lifetime of the metastable 3s 4P5/2 level: the Elsevier text of Levy et al. prints the unit with a symbol-font glyph ("ms"); it is microseconds, as the abstract of Shimizu et al. 2006 states explicitly (7.3 +- 0.5 us). The frequency of the 685.6 nm line is an old (1949) value quoted second-hand; treat it as a consistency check of the NIST Ritz value, not as a precision measurement. Sources were located through arXiv/DataCite, CORE, HAL, Crossref and publisher abstract pages; the web-search quota of the session was exhausted, so coverage is limited to what those indexes exposed.

transitions.use: 677.4 nm (air; 677.59 nm vac): open transition used for optical depopulation pumping of the metastable 3s 4P5/2 level (upper level also decays to 3s 4P3/2, which decays to the ground state); measurement of the metastable fraction of a neutralized F beam (Levy et al. 2007)

transitions.freq_src: hyperfine centre of gravity 14581.684 cm^-1 from Liden, Ark. Fys. 1, 229 (1949), as quoted and used for calibration in Levy, Cocolios, Behr, Jayamanna, Minamisono, Pearson, Nucl. Instrum. Methods A 580, 1571 (2007), Table 1 (collinear fast-beam LIF and modulated optical depopulation pumping)
transitions.use: 685.6 nm (air; 685.79 nm vac): closed (cycling) transition from the metastable 3s 4P5/2 level; suggested for laser cooling of metastable fluorine (Shimizu et al., Appl. Phys. B 72, 227 (2001)); optical pumping on it demonstrated in a fast F beam for nuclear-spin polarization (Levy et al. 2007); LIF line of the metastable-lifetime measurement (F=3 -> F'=4 component, Shimizu et al. 2006)
761 nm: diode-laser absorption hyperfine spectroscopy (Tate & Aturaliye 1997)
775 nm: diode-laser saturated-absorption hyperfine spectroscopy (Tate & Aturaliye 1997)
780 nm: diode-laser Doppler-free saturated-absorption hyperfine spectroscopy; absolute frequency of one hyperfine component measured against the Rb D2 line (Tate & Aturaliye, PRA 56, 1844 (1997))
